description:
## Observed problem

During the fz-tfn.26 current-base 502-test fixture matrix, matrix::spec_violation::run failed once reading a missing temporary telemetry file. Isolated rerun and a second parallel matrix passed unchanged. The historical failure does not establish its exact cause: a wall-clock filename collision is possible, not reproduced evidence.

## Goal

Each parallel fixture invocation exclusively owns a unique telemetry path from reservation through child completion, complete read, and cleanup.

## Traced ownership

The old helper derived an unreserved path from fixture stem, purpose, PID, and wall-clock nanoseconds; concurrent legs of the same fixture shared every component except the clock reading. Two consumers manually removed paths after reading, with no cleanup on early error or panic. The CLI creates/truncates the log before dispatch. Dispatch owns and drops the telemetry bus, flushing JsonlBackend before the CLI exits. The fixture command runner observes exit, tears down its command group, and reaps its child before returning output. No compiler semantic or flushing change is necessary.

## Implementation

FixtureTempFile generalizes the existing capture-file owner and its exclusive create_new allocation. Captures unlink immediately; telemetry keeps the name reserved. with_fixture_telemetry owns creation, running the command, strict final read, and checked normal unlink; RAII releases the name on command failure or unwinding. Remove the timestamp allocator, duplicated consumer reads, and manual telemetry cleanup. Existing allocation advances past already-existing candidate names; no read, command, or missing-file retry is introduced.

## TDD and acceptance

RED40698: fixture_telemetry_reserves_its_path failed deterministically against the old allocator because no file existed before spawning. GREEN47048: reservation/exclusive-create/drop test; command-error and panic cleanup plus injected missing-log hard error; and 24 simultaneous actual spec_violation invocations (8 each run/interp/build), distinct reserved paths, rejected compilation, every JSONL record parseable, expected typed diagnostic retained, and post-read cleanup.

Repeat the full parallel fixture matrix and relevant harness gates. No missing, reused, prematurely removed, or partially read telemetry under those runs. No sleep, timeout increase, command/read retry, ignored missing log, or compiler behavior change. Document temp-artifact ownership in .agent/docs/fixtures.md.

## Final verification

In progress: full parallel matrix and strict workspace/all-targets/all-features clippy. Fresh ticket-scoped cold review and all final gate evidence required before commit.
title: Give parallel fixture telemetry files collision-free lifecycle ownership
